source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 139 to 150. Each question cites its item. Authoring batch for the ITE pool; review before trusting.

questions.q: How long after intranasal naloxone is the peak plasma concentration reached?
questions.why: The clinical effect is often seen sooner than the peak. Anything that damages the nasal mucosa or its blood flow slows absorption.

questions.q: Breathing has recovered after naloxone. Why does monitoring continue?
questions.a: Its two-hour half-life is shorter than many opioids
d: A second dose is needed in every case
questions.why: A long-acting opioid outlasts the antidote, so respiratory depression can return as the naloxone wears off.

questions.q: A groin bulge that appears on straining and limits lifting at work. What is next?
d: CT of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.why: A hernia you can see or feel needs no imaging, and this one is symptomatic. Nearly half of patients sent for inguinal imaging did not need it.

questions.q: For which inguinal hernia is watchful waiting a reasonable option?
d: One with a dull ache at work
questions.why: Symptoms or limited function are what tip the decision to surgery. Appearing on straining is simply how a reducible hernia behaves.

questions.q: Memory decline, urgency with incontinence, a slow wide-based gait, enlarged ventricles, confirmed by high-volume lumbar puncture. Treatment?
questions.why: The triad with hydrocephalus is normal-pressure hydrocephalus, and the shunt relieves it. Donepezil treats Alzheimer disease, carbidopa-levodopa the Lewy body and Parkinson dementias, and levothyroxine the dementia of hypothyroidism.

questions.q: Which finding supports shunting in suspected normal-pressure hydrocephalus?
questions.a: A better gait after a high-volume lumbar puncture
d: A normal opening pressure on its own
Enlarged ventricles on MRI on their own
questions.why: The tap trial predicts response, which the imaging and the pressure cannot. Gait is the symptom that improves first and most.

questions.q: Painless gross haematuria in a 65-year-old on lisinopril, no fever or trauma. What is next?
d: A repeat urinalysis in a month
questions.why: Every adult with gross haematuria is referred, because the association with malignancy is strong and cystoscopy finds bladder cancer with 87 to 100 percent sensitivity. Cytology is too insensitive to stand in for it.

questions.q: Open questions, affirmations, reflective listening and summaries, to build autonomy in a smoker unsure about quitting. Which technique?
questions.why: The acronym OARS names the four components, and the method has level A evidence for weight, blood pressure and alcohol in primary care. BATHE and the five A's both use targeted, directive questions.

questions.q: Which model identifies how ready a patient is to change a behaviour?
questions.why: Precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action and maintenance are its stages. Knowing the stage helps choose the next technique, often motivational interviewing.

questions.q: In type 1 diabetes, a dusky red sharply bordered shin nodule that enlarges, flattens and develops a yellow-brown centre. Diagnosis?
questions.why: The evolving plaque with a yellow-brown centre is the giveaway, and its mechanism is still unclear. Eruptive xanthomas are clusters of small red-yellow papules on extensor surfaces and buttocks.

questions.q: Crops of brown atrophic patches on the shins of a long-standing diabetic. What are they?
questions.why: Dermopathy is pigmented and atrophic in crops; lipoatrophy is depressed but otherwise normal skin; rubeosis is a reddening of the face and limbs.

questions.q: Which deficiency does long-term metformin cause?
questions.why: In a placebo-controlled trial metformin lowered B12 levels by 19 percent and raised the absolute risk of deficiency by 7 percent, often without symptoms. Metformin is contraindicated in renal impairment but does not cause it.

questions.q: A well-looking 3-year-old with fever and left upper lobe consolidation. Which antibiotic?
questions.why: A focal consolidation points to pneumococcus or Haemophilus, and seven days of amoxicillin covers them. Cefdinir works but is broader than needed, and doxycycline is not used at this age.

questions.q: When is azithromycin the right choice for pneumonia in a child?
questions.a: When an atypical pneumonia is suspected
d: Any pneumonia with a fever over 39
questions.why: Mycoplasma and its relatives are the azithromycin targets. Most childhood pneumonia is viral and needs no antibiotic at all.

questions.q: A dorsal PIP dislocation, neurovascularly intact, with a fracture under 20% of the joint surface. What is done?
questions.a: Reduce, splint in flexion, buddy tape
d: Home, with radiographs in a week
questions.why: A simple stable dislocation is reduced in the office and splinted at about 30 degrees for two to four weeks, with films straight after reduction and at a week. Surgery is for the irreducible, the unstable and the badly displaced.

questions.q: Which features of a finger fracture-dislocation mean immediate surgical referral?
a: More than 30% of the articular surface involved
d: A fragment under 20% of the articular surface
questions.why: Malrotation, comminution, persistent subluxation, vascular compromise and loss of function complete the list. Pain and swelling are the injury, not indications.

questions.q: Greasy diarrhoea, cramps and nausea after backpacking in Nicaragua, stool positive for Giardia. Treatment?
questions.why: Metronidazole, tinidazole or nitazoxanide treat Giardia, and symptomatic patients are treated to shorten illness and stop spread. Azithromycin and ciprofloxacin are for bacterial travellers' diarrhoea.

questions.q: Which feature argues against Giardia as the cause of travellers' diarrhoea?
questions.why: Giardia gives greasy stools, pain and nausea after a one to two week incubation, and fever and vomiting are uncommon. Blood and fever point to an invasive bacterial cause.

questions.q: Depression in a patient with epilepsy. Which antidepressants are avoided for seizure risk?
questions.why: The four safer choices cover the SSRIs, the SNRIs and two others that do not lower the threshold. Bupropion is the one most often reached for by mistake.

questions.q: A healthy 20-year-old asks for cervical screening. What does the task force say?
questions.a: Not before 21; it is recommended against
d: Cytology now, then every three years
HPV testing now, then every five years
Co-testing now, then every five years
questions.why: Screening before 21 carries a D recommendation. What she is due at 20 is hepatitis C and HIV screening, and sun-protection counselling if her skin is fair.
